action: Place the probe at the posterior aspect of the heel to identify the insertion points.
interpretation: Visualize the calcaneus clearly. Identify the insertion point.

action: Identify the acoustic landmarks at the bone interface.
interpretation: Note the deep shadow underneath the calcaneus, confirming this as the attachment point of the Achilles tendon.

action: Maintain the probe in long-axis over the tendon.
interpretation: Observe the striations running across the screen, characteristic of tendon fibers.

action: Angle the probe slightly so the beam is not perpendicular to the fibers to demonstrate an artifact.
interpretation: Identify 'anisotropy,' a normal finding where the tendon appears as a hypoechoic area due to the angle of the probe.

action: Adjust the probe (heel-toe maneuver) to ensure the ultrasound beam is strictly perpendicular to the tendon.
interpretation: Confirm the hypoechoic area disappears when perpendicular. Recognize that the previous darkness was a normal artifact, not pathology or a tear.

action: Slide the probe proximally along the leg to visualize the full length of the tendon. Keep the tendon centered in the image.
interpretation: Visualize the longitudinal extent of the Achilles tendon.

action: Scan firmly along the tendon fibers.
interpretation: Inspect for interruptions in the fibers, complete disruption, or the presence of fluid.

action: Prepare to perform a quantitative assessment.
interpretation: Assess the actual thickness of the Achilles tendon.

action: Decrease the depth to optimize the view of the tendon. Freeze the image. Drop calipers to measure.
Take the measurement (resulting in approx 3.2mm). Compare this measurement to the contralateral side if available.
interpretation: Note the measurement is 3.2mm. Verify the finding as normal by comparing it to the unaffected side for an appropriate patient-specific baseline.

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees to a transverse orientation. Orient the probe marker pointing to the patient's left.
interpretation: Switch views to scan the Achilles tendon in a transverse orientation.

action: Center the structure in the field of view and resume scanning.
interpretation: Identify the Achilles tendon located in the center of the image.

action: Observe the internal echotexture of the tendon in the transverse plane.
interpretation: Visualize 'punctate hyperechoic structures' (dots). Confirm this as a normal transverse view.

action: Scan through the cross-section of the tendon.
interpretation: Screen for anechoic areas, interruptions, or complete disruption of the tendon structure.
Observe the morphology change as the tendon flattens out and transitions into muscle.
